2161.note: c. 46v margin checked at crop resolution (IIIF c12f9335). The clear note beside the four cipher lines reads about: 'por fas, o nefas se tenga cap[...] / d[...] en Cel[...] hasta / [...] se resuelua porq assi cumple / a V. Ex. y al Triu- / uirato il Pre y / a los hijos' (several words uncertain). It is the decipherment of those lines, or their clear draft: the cipher follows the clear words 'la qual' and opens with the signs 'Ao no n. mo a[?] . n. 9', which fit por fas o nefas. In key_1548.md no = r, mo = s and a-with-tail = o, and the 9-shaped sign looks like its s sign; the same dotted n stands at both 'fa' places, but the key has only fi for that family, and 'Ao' as po and the sign taken as ne are read from the margin, not the key. It closes 'e mo . q 3 mo', fitting lo-s hi-jo-s (key: e = lo, mo = s, 3 = jo; q as hi is not in the key). Only the opening and closing signs were compared, not the middle, and no full transcription was made, so this is strong evidence, not a proof.So on the leaf: c. 46v 4 lines with clear beside them; c. 40v one struck line with clear under it; c. 44r about 18 lines with no gloss (first pass's count, not re-counted). If the editions turn out not to print the letter, the verdict should separate these: the glossed passages are read on the leaf and c. 44r is what remains open. Searched this pass: Algunas cartas (snippets): 'abril 1549' gives pp. 126 and 123, the second a letter to Rodrigo de Mendoza from Simancas Estado 875, not this one; 'Modena', 'Estense', 'Campori', 'fas o nefas', 'Tapia', 'Telamon', 'Godines' 0 hits; 'Orbitello' pp. 328, 296, 324 and '3 de abril' pp. xxviii, xvii, xxi, none this letter. Losi (snippets): 'Ferrante 1549', 'cifra', 'Orbetello Tapia' 0; 'Massa' p. 65 only. Bertomeu Masia, La guerra secreta (2009, Google BqebtMQLd_MC, searchable with text snippets): its document index for 1549 (pp. 508-510) has letters to Granvela, its corpus, and 'Tapia', 'Orbitello', 'fas o nefas', 'Telamon' give 0, so it does not print this letter. Google Books search 'Ferrante Gonzaga' 'Hurtado de Mendoza' 'abril de 1549' carta cifra: no exact match. Cryptiana unsolved.htm: no Hurtado entry. known.py 'e02077fa', 'Campori', 'Hurtado de Mendoza', 'Ferrante Gonzaga': this lead and other Campori leads, no entry for this letter. Earlier first-pass evidence kept: all 14 canvases seen; signs of the Imperial Cipher family (mo, no, omega); slip c. 43 is a clear topic list, not a key; 4 web searches found no edition of this letter.

2183.note: Correction: Halm's 'in Chiffern' overstates it; the letter is clear German with long cipher passages. Numbers run about 11-36, which suggests a small substitution alphabet. Searches run: Anselm Casimir + Geleen + 22 Oct 1633; Geleen 1633 + Kurköln + intercepted; Bierther volume. None found a decipherment. No key tested. This pass, Google Books search-inside on eEPWsb6K5vEC, snippet-only: 'Camerariana' 0 (also 0 on 5a8yAQAAIAAJ), 'Clm 10406' 0, 'Geleen Chiffre' 0, 'Geleen chiffriert' 0, '1633 X 22 Geleen' 0, 'Kurmainz und Kurköln an Geleen' only pp. 844, 355, 688, none this letter, '22. Okt. 1633' only pp. 405, 969, 359. That suggests the edition did not use the Camerariana, but does not settle it, because p. 810 is unseen and each query is capped. The volume does take some letters to Geleen ('Menzel an [Geleen]', p. 844, 1634). Khevenhüller, Annales Tom. XII (MDZ bsb10866798, full-text API): Geleen on scans 579-590 as campaign narrative, 'Chiffre' and 'Ziffern' 0. Possible new lead, a different document: Bierther p. 405 (note in the snippet with Nr. 238, Kurmainz und Kurköln an Maximilian) cites a letter of 22 Oct as 'größtenteils in Chiffre, deren Auflösung jedoch fehlt', with a Richel summary in Kschw 5988/3 fol. 15; its sender is not visible in the snippet. Duplicates: known.py 'Clm 10406', 'Geleen', 'Anselm Casimir', 'Huyn': this lead, sibling n. 74/77 of the volume, and the Georg II of Hesse-Darmstadt catalogue entry, which is another series.

2184.note: Corrections: lead's shelfmark and MDZ links point to Clm 10416 / bsb00116464, the wrong volume. Salutation 'Rme Illme Princeps' and closing 'Rmae et Illmae Celsitudinis Vrae' are clear; dated 'Raptissime Osnabrugi 1633. 13 Aug.'; signed with initials I read as C. L. The address names a reverend prince, not an elector as such: Bishop Wartenberg, who had left for Bonn, is as possible as Elector Ferdinand. Faint marks over two lines look like show-through; check at colour resolution. Forst's Wartenberg correspondence ends 1631 from memory, not opened. Searches run: Osnabrück 13 Aug 1633 cipher; Clm 10415 + Chiffern; Bierther volume. None found a decipherment. No key tested. This pass: the two faint traces (over line 2 of the block, and over the line near the bottom that begins '410') were zoomed at 1000 px on the microfilm scan. They are pale, do not line up with the groups and could not be read; the scan cannot say whether they are show-through or erased gloss, so check a colour image if one is made. The edition evidence is search-inside on a snippet-only volume, as described in prior_art.edition.
